newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak short-term rates high, but not for long-NBS.
newsitem.headline: Slovak short-term rates high, but not for long-NBS.

text.p: The National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) said on Thursday it had considered the recent increase in the country's short-term interbank money market rates to the 15 percent level too high, but temporary.

"The current interest rates increase is a short-term phenomena, and we had expected such possibility...but they (rates) are really too high now, and we are interested in their decline," NBS governor Vladimir Masar told a news conference.
"But we also have to look at the price at which banks are interested in buying T-bills the yield for which had increased significantly," Masar added.
But he added the NBS has been considering "no new measures so far" to further tighten monetary policy, as it was waiting to see next year the full effect of its measures from mid-July.
In Wednesday's auction of Finance Ministry's 273-day treasury bills, the average yield hit 9.669 percent, up from 9.307 percent in the last at auction of similar T-bills.
Shortly after the auction, the NBS raised its bill repurchase rate by 70 basis points to 9.7 percent, but left the reverse repo rate unchanged at 7.2 percent.

"Unfortunately, this time the central bank only reacted (with the repo hike) to the market situation which had occured without the impetus from the NBS," Elena Kohutikova, head of the NBS monetary division, said.
